steps.body: In Grade 4 the ×10 ladder ran through the whole numbers: ×10 slid a digit one rung **left** (bigger), ÷10 one rung **right** (smaller). Nothing new happens at the decimal point — the same two moves keep working straight through it. The point is just a landmark, not a wall.

steps.body: Chaining moves just repeats the slide. Two ×10 moves is one rung left, then another: 0.03 → 0.3 → 3. Two ÷10 moves is two rungs right: 7 → 0.7 → 0.07. Count the moves, count the rungs.

explanationVariants: Two ×10 moves is two rungs left, landing on 3.

numericErrors.feedback: 0.3 is only one ×10 move. A second ×10 slides it one more rung left, to 3.
30 is three rungs left. There are only two ×10 moves here: 0.03→0.3→3.

widget.prompt: A value changed from 6 to 0.6. Which move did that?

choices.feedback: 6 to 0.6 slid one rung right and got ten times smaller — that's ÷10.
×10 makes a value ten times BIGGER (6 would become 60). Getting smaller, from 6 to 0.6, is ÷10.
Subtracting 5.4 does land on 0.6 here, but the ladder move that always turns 6 into 0.6 is ÷10 — one rung right.
÷100 is two rungs right (6 would become 0.06). One rung right, 6 to 0.6, is ÷10.

steps.body: One ladder, straight through the point.
takeaways: ×10 slides a digit one rung left (ten times bigger); ÷10 one rung right (ten times smaller).
The decimal point is a landmark, not a wall — the same moves cross it unchanged.
Chaining moves just counts rungs: two ×10 is two rungs left, three ÷10 is three rungs right.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **×10 makes a number ten times bigger and slides its digits one rung left; ÷10 makes it ten times smaller and slides them one rung right.** Example: 0.4 ×10 = 4 (left one rung), and 4 ÷10 = 0.4 (right one rung). Same ladder, opposite directions.

explanationVariants: 0.2 ×10 slides one rung left, into the ones place: 2.

choices.feedback: ×10 slides the 2 one rung left, from tenths to ones: 2.
0.02 is smaller — that's ÷10, the opposite move. ×10 makes 0.2 bigger: 2.
0.2 is unchanged. ×10 must slide the digit one rung left: 2.
